notes: Run with the skill-creator skill pointed at skills/bubbletea-tui. This file lives outside the skill on purpose: npx skills add copies the skill directory whole, and the prompts and graded assertions here must not reach the agent under evaluation. `files` are relative to the repository root. Each assertion is a failure seen when models build TUIs without the skill (or with an earlier version). Deterministic ones are checked by tuilint and the harness; the rest by a grader reading renders and the transcript. The init cases run unattended: an answers.md fixture stands in for the user. Add a case whenever the skill misses something in real use: write the miss as an assertion first, make the kit pass it, then edit the skill. An assertion that starts '(pair)' is graded only on a paired run: two cold builds of the case as the assertion describes them, judged side by side; a single run skips it.

evals.name: dashboard-from-brand-brief
evals.prompt: Build a Bubble Tea TUI for 'tidepool', a CLI that monitors background job queues (queues, workers, failed jobs, retries). Brand: deep sea green #0F5257 and coral #FF6F59, calm but precise, used by on-call engineers at 3am. I need a queue list, a detail view for the selected queue with throughput and failures, a retry confirmation, and an empty state. go run should start it.
evals.expected_output: A Bubble Tea v2 program with a tidepool theme JSON derived from the two hexes, a TUI.md, the harness flags, every state rendered and reviewed, and contact sheets shown.
assertions: imports charm.land/bubbletea/v2 and charm.land/lipgloss/v2 (no v1 imports)
go run ./cmd/<app> with no flags starts tea.NewProgram; -golden -w 80 -h 24 and -w 120 -h 40 exit 0
go test ./... passes in the app's module, the copied internal/ui and cmd/<app> tests included, on the app's own theme (they used to load the kit's themes by path and name)

a copied project whose only theme sets focus: fg (or expressions.spinner) passes go test ./... out of the box: the copied spinner test judges the Huh and Bubbles spinners by the theme's working ink (S.Working: fg under focus fg, the named role under spinner:), not by primary (it used to fail with `bubbles spinner renders "\x1b[38;2;207;205;202m..."` for a focus fg brand)
a themes/tidepool.json exists with dark and light roles derived from #0F5257 and #FF6F59; no hex literals outside the theme package (tuilint code C-HEX passes)

the brand read lives in TUI.md § Brand read (condensed in the theme's read field; no separate .read.md) and ties each expression choice it makes to a product trait, one line per expression, with no expression left unexplained

palette derive on the brand hexes exits 0 on its first run (its output passes its own check, even for a mid-tone primary such as #2E8B57), and palette check passes the shipped tidepool.json in dark and light with the brand's primary hex kept and no contrastAccept added for an on-colour
diversity shows the theme differs from kit ink on >= 8 axes

diversity was run with kit/themes/ink.json and kit/themes/charm.json among its inputs, so the min-distance rule actually ran (a --baseline name with no matching theme exits 2; it used to be skipped silently)

every role in themes/tidepool.json is #RRGGBB or #RGB with the # (no bare 0F5257, no #RRGGBBAA): theme.Load loads it and palette check exits 0, since Lip Gloss reads a value without # as an ANSI index or no colour
no rendered frame has emoji, library-default pink/purple, or more than one bordered box (tuilint frames passes)
tuilint frames passes on the -light, -ascii and -profile ansi256 renders too, not only dark truecolour (the footer bar, rules and 256-colour fallbacks break there first)
exactly one visible focus in every state, and the focus marker does not shift text
help is generated from key.Bindings; every key shown in a state's help works in that state
retry confirmation names the queue, focuses Cancel by default, and colours the action button as danger
empty state says what is missing, why in context, and the one key to fix it
at 120x40 a detail pane or extra section uses the room; at 80x24 it collapses to a summary
the agent rendered PNGs with cellshot and looked at them before replying

palette check passes the shipped theme including its glyphs: every glyph outside ASCII has an ASCII twin (glyphs.ascii or the kit's map) and no two state marks (done/current/todo/pending/partial, radio, check) share one, so a ◐ 'reading' and a ● 'new' never become the same * under -ascii

every dialog has a visible edge at -profile ansi and under NO_COLOR=1, not only in truecolour: a borderless panel one background step up lands on the page's colour there (the kit's dialog: none draws a rule above and below; dialog: rules always has one)
the -ascii renders pass tuilint frames --ascii (F-ASCII): no glyph outside ASCII leaks into an ASCII frame, and a cut footer ends in the full ...

under -ascii a cut line ends in ... (the theme's twin, or the sweep's three dots over the cut's last cells), never a lone . that reads as a full stop, never ~ (the partial mark's twin, which reads as a row in progress): every cut in a screen is ui.Trunc(t, ...) with t.G.Ellipsis, and tuilint code reports a bare theme.Ellipsis outside ui/ [C-ELLIPSIS]

under -ascii text keeps its letters and digits: a reading with a unit (21.5°C), a product (3×4) and an accented name (Zoë) draw 21.5 C, 3x4 and Zoe, never a ?, with no ASCII literal in the app's code; a rune whose one cell would change the value (± ≥ ≤ ‰ ³ ¬ †) stays ?, never a silent + > < % 3 - +; tuilint frames --ascii --unicode <the unicode frames> reports a ? cell where the unicode frame of the same state draws something else [F-ASCII]

a sentence-case brand with labelCase lower writes its sentences in sentence case: a canceled tool call reads Canceled. (t.Sentence takes titleCase for the kit's sentences; t.Copy takes labelCase for every label, so a two-word tab name such as Pull requests sits in the same case as its one-word neighbours), never canceled. at the head of a line

a tool body with go test output (ok  \tpkg\t0.412s) keeps the panel's right edge: the kit's Fit, Trunc and Canvas.Draw expand a tab to its 8-column stop before measuring, with no tab replacement in the app's code

a brand spinner wider than one cell (··· •·· ••· •••) keeps its width and shape under -ascii (... :.. ::. ::: or the next free cells), never the one-cell line spinner, and no ASCII frame holds a status, bar or caret mark's twin

the state ladder (queued, running, retrying, failed, done) draws its marks from the theme's status slots, never literals: in progress is t.G.Partial (◐, ascii ~), not current's ● in another colour, so under NO_COLOR and -ascii every rung keeps its own shape

a theme whose state roles collide at 16 colours carries an ansi16 pin: palette check on the shipped theme prints no 16-colour clash (stderr), e.g. a warning #E9B949 and an error #E0665C that both downsample to ANSI 9 at -profile ansi get "ansi16": {"dark": {"warning": 11}}, and a brand whose hue is a state (focus fg) never shares primary's slot with error; the brand hexes stay as derived

palette check passes the shipped theme with no unknown expression key or value (it exits 2 on "dialog": "rule" for "rules" and lists what the kit knows): every expression the brand read chooses is one the kit draws, none silently falls back to a default
a running job's working mark in the status column is one cell like the dots beside it (ui.Busy, not a multi-cell spinner), and under -ascii it is never the focus bar's | or another state's mark

every toggle's help names what the key does now: a key that pauses while following reads `f pause`, not `f follow`, in the state where the header or status says following (render both states; the footer and the status word never show the same verb)

the critic round was a fresh subagent given the PNGs and goldens, or, with no subagent tool, a fresh message that re-read only the PNGs and goldens with verify.md's prompt, and the hand-off says which; a self-review with the code in context is not a critic
go vet -vettool=$(which tuivet) ./... (or tuivet ./...) exits 0 in the app's module: the tuilint code rules hold as go/analysis analyzers too, so an editor or CI run finds nothing tuilint code didn't

tuilint code on the project reports no C-GLYPH: every mark the screens draw (the input caret, the scrolled-off marker, separators, arrows, progress and status glyphs) is a theme glyph (t.G.Caret, t.G.Sep, t.G.More, t.G.Arrow), not a string literal; text (quotes, dashes, units) is left alone

tuilint frames judges the inside of the retry confirmation, whatever the dialog style: under a bordered, +--+ (ascii) or rules dialog the frames carry no 'checked only by eye' note, and a low-contrast cell inside the panel would fail F-CONTRAST; a dialog: none theme justifies the note in one line

every role a dialog draws (border, borderFocus, bgPanel, bgOverlay) lands on a grey at -profile ansi, whatever tint the theme wrote, so a ruled or bordered dialog's edge never draws in error's red there: palette check exits 1 on a borderFocus pin that lands on red (1/9) and warns on one that lands on another hue (a borderFocus #746B5A on #17140F used to downsample to ANSI 1 with check saying OK)

palette derive on an amber brand (#D99A3B on #17140F / #F6F1E6) pins primary to yellow 11 on the dark page with warning on the other yellow, 3, and to fg's grey 0 on the light page (no hue: yellow 3 is unreadable on white) with warning keeping yellow 3, never primary to green 10 or magenta 5 and never warning to green, blue or cyan; palette check warns when a pin (the theme's or derive's) moves a role more than 60 degrees of OKLCH hue from its truecolour hex while a nearer slot is free, naming the hex, its hue and the slot

a warm brand (palette derive "#C2622B", copper, or coral #D15D51) never draws on magenta 5/13 or error's red at -profile ansi, nor do its secondary, tertiary or accent: dark pins primary 11 and warning 3, light pins primary 0 and the -light -profile ansi render draws focus in fg and bold; palette check exits 1 on a theme that pins primary to yellow 11 with a white fgSelected (1.17:1 in cellshot's palette), on a warning pinned to green, and on a primary pinned to yellow 3 on a light page; every warning mark (a degraded row's sparkline included) carries the warn glyph

tuilint frames --ascii on the -ascii renders judges a rule drawn in ASCII twins (a rules dialog's `-- title -----`, a `=====` progress bar, a `-----` tab underline) as decoration, the way ─ ━ ▔ are: the two-cell lead of a titled rule at 2.29:1 on the panel is no F-CONTRAST, the same cells as letters are (the theme is never darkened to get a rule past a text floor)

palette check fails a border under 1.3:1 on its bg and warns under 1.5:1 (it used to pass 1.14, rules nobody can see); palette derive's border lands at 1.5-1.9, and the shipped theme's section, table and footer rules are visible on the dark and light sheets while still quiet
the kit's README copy block leaves a gofmt-clean tree: gofmt -l . prints nothing right after the copy (the perl import rewrite used to leave cmd/<app>/main.go's imports out of order)

palette check exits 2 on a spinner whose multi-cell frames contain a status or focus mark (frames `··· •·· ••· •••` beside a pending `·`): every rune of every frame is compared, not only a one-cell frame as a whole

in a project that keeps the skill as a .claude/skills link into .agents/skills, a reinstall is `npx skills experimental_install`, never `npx skills add`, which replaces the link with a copy and leaves .agents/skills at the old version

a product whose states are not the kit's (new, reviewed) declares them as the theme's `ladder` ([{glyph, meaning, role}]: glyph a status slot name or a literal with an ASCII twin, role a colour role): the `ladder` frame draws those rungs in their inks, `ui.Mark(t, "new")` draws the same rung, and palette check fails a rung whose role or glyph the kit doesn't know; `ui.Dot(t, "ok")` is the done rung, so ● never means both now (current) and healthy

a blurred chat turn carries its bar in muted, never the focus ink: in the assistant-busy frame (input disabled) no turn bar is bold or focus-coloured, so under NO_COLOR and -ascii the screen shows no focus that isn't there

the blurred selection gutter (theme.Styles.BlurBar: an unfocused list or table under a dialog) draws in fgSubtle, ≥ 2.3:1 on bg in both modes, not bgSubtle (about 1.2:1, invisible at truecolour and a bare | under NO_COLOR told from the focused one by bold alone)

the clock ticks only while a visible cell changes (Law 8): a theme whose spinner frames are wider than one cell draws a deploying row as the still partial mark and the clock stops (ui.BusyAnimates), and -ascii agrees with unicode for that theme (both animate a one-cell spinner, or both hold the partial mark)

the kit's fixed copy follows the theme's case: tab names, 'Terminal too small', a tool call's 'Canceled.' and 'Waiting for permission', Thinking's 'Thought for': the labels (tab and step names, one word or several) take labelCase when set, else titleCase, and the sentences take titleCase (quire: `services / pull requests / deploys`, `Canceled.`); Huh field titles are the app's own text, written in the brand's case by the app

a dialog never reaches the footer: ui.Dialog takes the rows it may use and scrolls its body (an ↑ n more row above, a … n more row below) when it doesn't fit, so the help dialog at 80×24 and 60×18 ends at least one row above the footer rule in every theme, with ↑↓ in its footer only when there is more to see

an overlay's rows are its own at every size: at 120×40 in truecolour no page text stands on the rows a dialog spans (no `…`-cut fragment such as `…to show it` beside it), and the page above and below shows dimmed

where the page can't be dimmed (-profile ansi, -light -profile ansi, NO_COLOR=1, -ascii -profile ansi) the page's body is hidden behind a centred dialog, at 80×24 and 120×40: no page text at full ink above, below or beside it (a confirm over a composer never shows the composer's text under its edge), while the header above the body stays

a dialog whose body must be shown whole and has no length bound (a write's verbatim text) is listed in the harness's scrolls table, scrolls between edges that stay, and draws its position while rows are hidden (`lines 1–10 of 76` in its bottom edge via ui.DialogLines, or Clip's ↑/… n more rows); every other overlay fits the floor uncut

ASCII twins never collide across meanings: the input caret's twin (▏ → ') is not the focus bar's |, and the ASCII sparkline ramp holds no status twin (no * or +), so a caret never reads as a focused block and a peak never as a done or current mark

the footprint test renders every ordinary state at the floor TUI.md § Size floor names (60×18 unless the product raised it) and the four sizes above it, and one size below the floor asserts the too-small screen; a product with an 80×24 floor does not keep the kit's 60×18 list, where toosmall renders and passes as a layout

with themes/<brand>.json already written by brand, craft's copy skipped the `<closest>.json` line of the README block (the derived roles were not overwritten by a kit donor's), and once its screens were in it deleted what the README names as the showcase's alone (data.go and screens_test.go; setup.go and setup_test.go with their scrSetup, m.setup and setup-* wiring), set main.go's states, overlays, overlayPages, unjudgedPages and openOverlay to its own (unjudgedPages holding only form pages whose focus can't be drawn blurred, never the main screen, each reason repeated in TUI.md § Decisions; a page that is a variant of a judged one is in overlayPages or renders as it), and kept showcase_test.go, overlay_test.go, behaviour_test.go and ansi16_test.go whole, none of them edited to name its states, tests deleted or skipped; go vet, go test ./... and tuilint code pass after the delete

every expression axis moved after a diversity failure carries its product reason in the brand read and TUI.md § Decisions, and none reads 'to pass diversity' or 'for the distance' as its only reason: an axis the lint alone moved (a scrim dropped, a dialog edge swapped) was moved back and the distance found in a move the read asked for

TUI.md § Brand read names a move, one region elsewhere in the screen's order than the kit's default puts it (above or below a different region, left or right of one), or gone, or added, traced to 'calm but precise' (e.g. the failing queue's detail leads above the list; status is one sentence under the list, not header details), and a signature, one element the kit doesn't draw by default (e.g. a cell-art mark, a depth gauge beside the name); the two are different regions, and neither is a restyle: a glyph, a rule style, a hue or an expression value that restyles a region (`"header": "stamp"` is paint; a one-row shift from a gap, `density` or `footer: rule` is not a move, and a rule row a theme expression adds is not an added region; one that removes a region or puts it elsewhere in the screen's order is a move)

the main screen's default frame as rendered (the queue list with nothing pressed) shows the brand read's move and its signature, not only the sketch or a state the user has to reach, and the screen's § Screens block names that frame; the moved region is not where the kit's showcase puts it (a header row with the name and context, the list leading, status in the header and the footer)

TUI.md § Screens gives every block after the main screen's (the queue detail, the retry confirmation, the empty state, help) one `brand:` line saying what 'calm but precise' changes on that screen: its copy voice, its dialog form or its footer phrasing, or 'nothing, because …' with the reason; each follows from the brand's words and is judged by what a user reads, not by paint (a theme expression, a hue or a glyph is not a brand line), and the built screen shows it; the main screen's block comes first, and tuilint spec raises no S-SLOTS

(pair) graded only on a paired run; skip it on a single build. Built twice from this prompt by separate cold agents, once as written and once with 'calm but precise' replaced by 'terse, blunt, fast' (same hexes): a reader given both briefs, with names and hue withheld, can tell which brief each build's detail-view footer, retry-confirmation question, buttons and footer came from, and both confirms still name the queue and what the retry changes. Fails: the two confirms or footers read the same, or differ only by a synonym or a key that no brief word explains, or share a sentence that neither the prompt nor the kit wrote (two brands built from one monitor spec matched each other's main screens in nothing and their detail, picker and confirm word for word, down to one invented line about what the signal does)

a stacked pair at 80×24 (the queue list over its detail, or a summary over a log) shares rows by content, the upper taking what it fills and the lower the rest: no region holds five or more blank rows while the one under it cuts content
at 80×24 the queue list (the surface the user acts on) keeps at least half the body rows; the throughput and failure readings above or beside it fold onto shared rows before taking rows from the list

a throughput or failure sparkline drawn taller than one row grows upward from its label's row: the label, the current value and the bar's base share the bottom row and the peaks rise above it; the label is never on one row with the bar alone on the next

a reading past its warning level (a failure rate or retry ratio in the amber band) carries the theme's warn mark beside its value and a reading in the error band the fail mark, so the band survives NO_COLOR and 16 colours where amber is the text colour or red's slot; the ladder frame shows both marks

the queue poll is a product clock with its own message and gen, separate from the frame clock: the handler that changes its interval or pauses and resumes it returns the new arm cmd (never a gen bump alone), the poll keeps running when a spinner starting or stopping bumps the frame clock's gen, and a behaviour test like the kit's TestClockSurvivesSettingChange delivers the armed tick and asserts it syncs and re-arms

a history with a fixed range (a failure %, worker utilisation) is drawn with ui.Trace on that range (TraceOpts Min/Max), not ui.Sparkline or a hand-written trace: an idle or 4-9 % history draws one even row of braille dots (⣀), never a solid ▁ hairline or the section rule's glyph, a series of zeros draws it a step quieter (fgSubtle), cells before the first sample are blank, and a one-sample spike survives Per samples a cell

a selected row under selection fill or inverse keeps its fill through a sparkline or trace cell at truecolour and at -profile ansi: the bars draw in a shade of the fill (ui.Table, Styles.SelBars), never in the row's ink, which on most themes is the page and punches ▆▇█ holes through the bar; a blurred selected row keeps bgSubtle under every cell; under NO_COLOR every cell of the row is reversed and the bars stay as marks on it

the too-small screen is drawn by ui.TooSmall, or by ui.TooSmallText when the spec words it (its sentence, sizes included, wrapped and centred), never a hand-written tooSmall; a spec that asks for the sentence and nothing else gets no key row (no enabled binding in the toosmall row) and the copied TestTooSmallKeysAreTheTable still passes
under titleCase lower a dialog or section title keeps a word in capitals as written ("send SIGTERM to 13912?", "CPU", "3 PRs"); the agent never moves an acronym out of a title to dodge the case
section lines are ui.Section, with a styled span in the info where a figure needs its own ink (a red band, an fg figure), never a hand-written copy of Section to escape its subtle info
a dense table (8 columns or more at 80 cells) is ui.Table with its gap argument (1) rather than hand-written rows for tighter gaps
a footer key that names one arrow ("↓ select") takes it from the theme (t.G.Down, t.G.Up: ↓ ↑, ASCII v ^), not a literal, and passes tuilint code's C-GLYPH
a throughput or latency sparkline shows a +20 % step as a step (two or more glyphs, below full height), while ±5 % noise draws the quiet floor

confirms by consequence: TUI.md places the retry on a rung of the confirm ladder with its reason, and the build matches it. On rung 4 (a retry is normally safe here) the confirmation opens only on a failing signal, the queue's failure rate in the error band or the jobs failing every attempt with the same error, names it in the question ('Retry 214 jobs in payments? 96% failed with the same timeout'), and a retry with no such signal runs on its key with a toast naming what was retried; on rung 3 (a bulk retry can't be taken back, e.g. it could charge a customer twice) it always confirms and names what can't be taken back. Either way a harness state renders the retry confirmation, so the other assertions on it have a state to grade

if the app can purge or discard failed jobs (or delete a queue), that action confirms: the question names the queue and the count, says the jobs can't be brought back, and Cancel is focused; if it can pause or resume a queue, that is one key with no confirm, the row shows it at once, and the same key (its help now reading resume) undoes it

every confirm's question names the one thing the user is judging: the object and what can't be taken back ('Purge 214 failed jobs from payments? They can't be brought back.') or the failing signal ('96% failed with the same timeout. Retry anyway?'); none asks 'Are you sure?' or 'Continue?', a question that fits any action and so asks for no judgement

a theme that sets scrim: none chose it knowing a centred dialog then hides the page's body rows (header and footer stay) in every profile: the brand read or TUI.md § Decisions says so, and no § Screens brand: line or decision promises that the page stays readable behind the retry confirmation; a brand that needs the queue list readable behind a dialog keeps scrim: dim, and says it stays readable at truecolour and 256 colours only, since at 16 colours and NO_COLOR nothing dims and the body hides under either value

each secondary screen's render does what its § Screens brand: line says, read side by side: no line promises a wording, a placement or an absence its frame contradicts (a line saying 'no descriptions' over a picker that draws one, a sentence the line quotes that the dialog words differently), and the critic's round names any line and frame that disagree; the fix moves the render or rewrites the line, never leaves both

every page that draws a focus mark (each overlayPages state) and every overlay but help binds a help key in its own action table: `? help`, or `ctrl+g help` where a focused text box types ?, so the kept TestHelpOverAnOverlayNamesItsKeys finds one with no edit; no focused page is left out of overlayPages to dodge it

the four kept harness tests (showcase_test.go, overlay_test.go, behaviour_test.go, ansi16_test.go) sit in the package that holds the root model and the harness tables and pass there; if that package is not cmd/<app>'s package main (an existing app's internal/app), the copy changed only their package clause, and go test ./... runs them rather than skipping, deleting or rewriting one

TUI.md § Brand read carries a skeleton: line declaring the main screen's default frame as built (head, status, order, foot, verdict, chart, chartGlyphs, turnEnd, each one of diversity's words or - for an axis the screen doesn't have), and diversity was run with TUI.md among its inputs (diversity TUI.md kit/themes/ink.json kit/themes/charm.json …) with no P2 note for a missing line, axis or unknown word; read against the rendered default frame axis by axis, no value contradicts it, and no word was changed in the line without the frame changing to pass the lint

when the build hits a miss in the skill, the kit or a tool (a reference the kit contradicts, a kept test or lint that fires on a correct frame, a component it had to write by hand, a tool too slow for the loop), the agent offers feedback (references/cmd-feedback.md) once, at a natural stop (the hand-off, or the critic's ship), not mid-task; it dedupes first (feedback similar), shows the exact draft from feedback draft verbatim before anything is sent, files nothing (no feedback submit, gh issue create or --open) without the user's yes to that draft, and the draft holds none of the user's names or paths: the app's name, its brand words and the project path are replaced (--redact, <project>) and the agent says what it redacted. In an unattended run with no user to answer, the transcript shows the offer and the draft and no issue filed

evals.name: agent-chat-like-crush
evals.prompt: I want a chat UI for my coding agent in the terminal, as nice as Crush but not a copy of it. Brand name 'loom', colours violet #7C5CFF on near-black, but we want it to feel warmer and more editorial than Crush.
evals.expected_output: A chat TUI with messages, tool calls in the Crush grammar, a working animation, an editor, and an identity that differs from the charm study theme.
assertions: tool calls use status glyph + name + main param + k=v options and an indented panel body; a collapsed tool call shows the hidden line count and the key that expands it
one shared animation clock that stops when idle (tick returns nil in idle states)
the working indicator says what is happening (no 'Loading...'/'Thinking...' alone without subject or elapsed time)
diversity: loom differs from the charm study theme on >= 8 axes (not Crush recoloured)
prose is capped at a measure (<= 100 cells) at 200 columns
editor uses a real cursor via tea.View.Cursor
the brand read ties 'warm' and 'editorial' each to a named expression axis and its value (e.g. editorial → titleCase lower, measure 72; warm → a tinted neutral, a soft motif), not to a colour alone

if the brand read makes the type lowercase, the theme says so for labels too (expressions.labelCase "lower"): table headers, tags and toast labels follow it, and no kit-forced SERVICE or SETUP is left on screen

a body viewer (tool output, code, JSON, a response) draws its text at two lightnesses, names or keys in fg and punctuation or values in muted, not at one flat level and not as a rainbow of per-token colours

TUI.md § Brand read names a move, one region elsewhere in the screen's order than the kit's chat puts it (above or below a different region, left or right of one), or gone, or added, traced to 'warm' or 'editorial' (where the session facts live, what ends a turn, whether there is a header row), and a signature, one element the kit doesn't draw by default (a cell-art mark, a composition the kit doesn't ship); the two are different regions, and neither is a restyle: a glyph, a rule style, a hue or an expression value that restyles a region (`"header": "stamp"` or `"bar"` is paint; a one-row shift from a gap, `density` or `footer: rule` is not a move, and a rule row a theme expression adds is not an added region; one that removes a region or puts it elsewhere in the screen's order is a move), so two brands on one spec don't both land on a dashed rule

the chat's main state at 80×24, rendered from the app's harness on a fixture with one finished turn (a user message, a tool call, the reply), shows the move and the signature. Reference: the kit's chat in its baseline theme, `go -C <skill>/kit run ./cmd/showcase -theme themes/ink.json -state assistant -w 80 -h 24`, so a row that loom's `expressions` move shows against it. Passes: at least one of the header row, the session facts, the turn-end row, the rule above the input or the footer sits elsewhere in the screen's order than in the reference (above or below a different region, left or right of one), or is gone, or is added. Judged by effect, whatever does it (app code or an `expressions` value). Fails: the listed regions keep their order and only their style differs (a glyph, a rule style, a hue, `"header": "stamp"` or `bar`), or they shift a row from a gap, `density` or `footer: rule`, or the only added row is a rule a theme expression draws (terrarium against ink moves the turn-end row and the input rule up one and adds a footer rule, with no app change: that fails) (two brands built from one spec on the kit used to share all of them to the cell)

a message typed in the composer is sent by its send key with no second 'Send this?' prompt and no confirm state: the send is the confirmation; a confirm appears only for what can't be undone (discarding a long draft, deleting a session), never for a send

evals.name: init-keys-and-glyphs
evals.prompt: I'm not available; read answers.md and take the proposed default for anything it doesn't answer. /bubbletea-tui init — SPEC.md describes the TUI we're building. Interview me and write TUI.md.
evals.expected_output: A TUI.md that keeps what SPEC.md decided and catches what it got wrong for a terminal: indistinguishable keys, a global key a text box eats, one accent with three meanings, ambiguous-width state dots, footers that overflow 80 columns, dialogs that vanish without colour. It passes tuilint spec.
assertions: no key that terminals without key disambiguation deliver as another key (shift+enter, ctrl+enter, ctrl+m, ctrl+i, ctrl+[, ctrl+backspace …) is advertised in TUI.md's key table without a fallback in the same cell (e.g. `shift+enter/ctrl+j newline`), although SPEC.md asks for Shift+Enter; tuilint spec reports no S-KEYAMBIG

the ctrl+k quick switcher is not a global key in the reply and note states, where a Bubbles textarea deletes to end of line on ctrl+k: it is rebound, or those states bind it explicitly; tuilint spec reports no S-KEYSHADOW for it

the brand read gives each accent hue exactly one meaning, and focus is not drawn in the unread colour, so the inbox cursor row and an unread row look different, although SPEC.md asks amber to mean unread, focus and the active filter

each state dot (● ◐ ○) has an ASCII twin named in TUI.md, and the brand read says how the dots stay width-safe in the inbox's state column (they are East Asian Width ambiguous); tuilint spec reports no S-GLYPHWIDTH
TUI.md says how focus, selection and errors stay visible under -profile ascii and lists the colour profiles it supports (truecolor, 256, 16, none)
the key table has a partial state for the inbox (one of Forge, Beacon or mail failed while the others loaded), besides its empty, loading and error states
the ● ◐ ○ ✓ state ladder keeps ◐: it has an ASCII twin and sits in a 2-cell column, and is not dropped or replaced by plain text for being ambiguous-width

no state's footer keys overflow the 80-column footer: a state with more actions than fit (the inbox) marks its footer (bold keys, or ‖ after them), keeping its main actions and its way out in it and the rest reachable from ? help; tuilint spec reports no S-FOOTER

TUI.md's colour line says what separates dialogs and overlays from the page where the background step is gone (16 colours, NO_COLOR, -profile ascii), e.g. a hairline rule or border, although SPEC.md asks for borderless filled panels

tuilint spec reports no S-ACCENT on TUI.md: once the accents: line gives the hue its one meaning (amber = new), no other line puts 'the accent' or 'the primary hue' on the wordmark, a spinner, a ramp or anything else; a brief that does trips S-ACCENT and is fixed before the hand-off

every overlay state's harness name in the key table carries one of dialog, palette, confirm, modal, overlay, popup, help or keys (confirm-discard, not discard; quick-switcher-palette, not switcher), because tuilint frames finds a ruled, ASCII or borderless dialog only by its name and otherwise lints the scrimmed page behind it, failing F-CONTRAST on every dimmed cell

every marked row with help-only keys shows its own help key: `? help`, or `ctrl+g help` in the Reply and Note rows, whose text boxes type `?`; Global binds no ctrl+g, which a focused textarea takes as select-all (no S-KEYSHADOW), and a confirm row with `y yes` either shows every key or ends `? help` (no S-FOOTER); each key cell is `key action` items, one binding per item with the key first (`ctrl+c twice quit now`)

TUI.md § States and keys gives mark done, snooze and bulk mark-done no confirm state: each happens on its key, the row shows it at once, and the same key or the undo key in a toast that names what happened ('Marked 12 done · u undo') takes it back, that undo key bound in the action table while the toast shows; a confirm-* state exists only for an action that can't be undone or is risky in that state, and its § Screens block says which

Reply and Note are sent by their send key (enter) with no confirm state and no 'Send this reply?' prompt: the send is the confirmation (the user judged the text while writing it), so no confirm guards it

if TUI.md keeps a send that can't be recalled (a reply to mail over IMAP, a page), it sends on its send key with no confirm state: composing and sending was the judgement. It gets a grace-window state by default ('Sending to ops@ in 5 s · u undo'): the send is held ~5 s under an undo toast whose undo key is in the action table. TUI.md may skip the window only for a send where seconds matter, and then says so in one line with the reason. Either way, a confirm appears only when a failing signal makes the send risky
